title: Integral adjunction normalization and transport of tower transpose equations
statement:
Fix the global datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\geq1$. All schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ for the ordinary derived category of strict varying-coefficient towers restricted to constructible levels with common finite cohomological and Tor intervals [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Write $r^D_{n,m}:D_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\to D_m$ for its derived reduction map, $m\leq n$ [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]; normalized means all these maps are invertible.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $v:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary, and put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $u:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$. Fix a compactification $f=pj$ and its pullback for $f'$ [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. Write $F_f=Rf_{!,\bullet}$, $G_f=f^!_\bullet$, and similarly $F_{f'},G_{f'}$, for the tower operations and adjunctions of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels, det-sp-tower-gluing]. Their units and counits are $\eta_f,\varepsilon_f$ and $\eta_{f'},\varepsilon_{f'}$.

Now take $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\mathcal I_T=\Dbc(T,\mathbf Z_\ell)$, with completed coefficient sheaves, and use the reduction/limit equivalences $r_T\dashv L_T$, units $\iota_T$ and counits $\kappa_T$ of [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. Write $h^*_I$ for completed integral pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and $F_{f,I}=Rf_{!,\mathbf Z_\ell}$ for the separately derived compactification functor of [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower]. Let $J_f=f^!_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ be its specified right adjoint [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. For $H_f=L_XG_fr_Y$, with its transported adjunction from [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection], there is a unique counit-preserving natural isomorphism $\delta_f:J_f\xrightarrow{\sim}H_f$, and likewise for $f'$. Under these identifications the integral counits reduce to tower counits, using the entire-tower comparisons
$$r_YF_{f,I}\simeq F_fr_X,\qquad r_XJ_f\simeq G_fr_Y,$$
and likewise for $f'$. Denote the integral counits by $\varepsilon_{f,I},\varepsilon_{f',I}$.

For $K\in\mathcal I_Y$ put $P_K=u_\bullet^*G_fr_YK$, $Q_K=G_{f'}v_\bullet^*r_YK$. Let
$$a_K:r_{X'}(u_I^*J_fK)\xrightarrow{\sim}P_K,\qquad b_K:r_{X'}(J_{f'}v_I^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_K$$
be the composites of $\delta_f,\delta_{f'}$, their reduction comparisons, and the completed-pullback reconstruction counits $\alpha$ specified in [lem-sp-ctf-tower-pullback-reconstruction]. The towers $P_K,Q_K$ are normalized, using [det-sp-tower-gamma](3). Fix the compactification exchange $\beta:v_\bullet^*F_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{f'}u_\bullet^*$. For $M\in\mathcal I_X$, let $\beta_I(M)$ be its unique coefficient transport with
$$r_{Y'}\beta_I(M)=\beta(r_XM)$$
under the displayed direct-image and pullback comparisons. Such an integral isomorphism exists uniquely.

For any natural actual tower morphism $t_K:P_K\to Q_K$, define its integral reconstruction $T_K:u_I^*J_fK\to J_{f'}v_I^*K$ by
$$T_K=\iota_{J_{f'}v_I^*K}^{-1}\circ L_{X'}(b_K^{-1}t_Ka_K)\circ\iota_{u_I^*J_fK}.$$
It satisfies $r_{X'}T_K=b_K^{-1}t_Ka_K$. Under the same full-tower operation comparisons, the reduction of its integral transpose is exactly
$$r_{Y'}\bigl(\varepsilon_{f',I,v_I^*K}\circ F_{f',I}(T_K)\bigr)=\varepsilon_{f',\bullet,v_\bullet^*r_YK}\circ F_{f'}(t_K).$$
Consequently, if $t$ satisfies the tower counit equation
$$\varepsilon_{f',\bullet}\circ F_{f'}(t_K)=v_\bullet^*(\varepsilon_{f,\bullet,r_YK})\circ\beta(G_fr_YK)^{-1},$$
then its reconstruction satisfies the integral counit equation
$$\varepsilon_{f',I}\circ F_{f',I}(T_K)=v_I^*(\varepsilon_{f,I,K})\circ\beta_I(J_fK)^{-1}.$$
No invertibility of $t$ is assumed, and these are equalities of actual morphisms under the specified reconstruction comparisons.

source.place: Proof (3), right-adjoint normalization, reconstruction comparisons and identification of the integral transpose

proof.text: The base-changed map $f'$ is smooth of the same relative dimension $d$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1); the pulled-back compactification is a compactification by [def-cbc-compact-support-square]. By [lem-sp-ctf-tower-pullback-reconstruction] all schemes here are Noetherian, and pullback preserves normalized constructible towers. Thus [det-sp-normalized-equivalence] applies at every vertex, with invertible unit $\iota$ and counit $\kappa$. From now on take $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and abbreviate $u_\bullet^*,v_\bullet^*$ to $U,V$. All comparisons below are natural maps in the ordinary tower derived category.

source.place: Proof (3), right-adjoint normalization, reconstruction comparisons and identification of the integral transpose

proof.text:
The left adjoint of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] is the integral compact support $Rf_!M=R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{!,n}(M/\ell^n)$ of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], not literally $F_{f,I}=R\bar f_*j_!$. Clause (2) of [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower] gives the canonical natural isomorphism $\phi_f:F_{f,I}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!$ on $\mathcal I_X$. Transport along it: $F_{f,I}\dashv J_f$ on $\mathcal I_X,\mathcal I_Y$ with counit $\varepsilon_{f,I,K}=\varepsilon^{J}_{f,K}\circ\phi_{f,J_fK}$, where $\varepsilon^J_f$ is the counit of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]; this is the adjunction meant by "its specified right adjoint". By [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection], the same $F_{f,I}$ has right adjoint $H_f=L_XG_fr_Y$, with the displayed Hom bijection. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to these two adjunctions, obtaining the unique natural isomorphism $\delta_f:J_f\to H_f$ with $\varepsilon^H_{f,K}F_{f,I}(\delta_{f,K})=\varepsilon_{f,I,K}$. Repeat for $f'$. Write $\sigma_{f,M}:r_YF_{f,I}M\xrightarrow{\sim}F_fr_XM$ for the entire-tower comparison of [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower], and $q_{f,K}=\kappa_{X,G_fr_YK}\,r_X(\delta_{f,K}):r_XJ_fK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_fr_YK$. The Hom bijection sends $g$ to $L_X(h)\iota_M$ with $h$ the tower transpose of $r_Y(g)\sigma_{f,M}^{-1}$; following $\mathrm{id}_{H_fK}$ back gives $h=\kappa_{X,G_fr_YK}$, hence $r_Y(\varepsilon^H_{f,K})=\varepsilon_{f,\bullet,r_YK}F_f(\kappa_{X,G_fr_YK})\sigma_{f,H_fK}$. Reducing the counit-preserving equation and using naturality of $\sigma_f$ at $\delta_{f,K}$ gives, as actual tower maps,
$$r_Y(\varepsilon_{f,I,K})=\varepsilon_{f,\bullet,r_YK}\,F_f(q_{f,K})\,\sigma_{f,J_fK}.$$
The same equation holds for $f'$. This uses the full-tower Hom bijection, not an inference from equality at every level.

source.place: Proof (3), right-adjoint normalization, reconstruction comparisons and identification of the integral transpose

proof.text:
Fix $K$, put $R=r_YK$, $C=u_I^*J_fK$, $D=J_{f'}v_I^*K$, and write $q=q_{f,K}$. The pullback comparison $\alpha$ of [lem-sp-ctf-tower-pullback-reconstruction] and Step 2 give precisely
$$a_K=U(q)\,\alpha_{u,J_fK},\qquad b_K=G_{f'}(\alpha_{v,K})\,q_{f',v_I^*K}.$$
The tower $R$ is normalized by [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. By [det-sp-tower-gamma](3), $G_fR$ is normalized constructible; pullback preservation makes $P_K=UG_fR$ normalized constructible. Likewise $VR$ and $Q_K=G_{f'}VR$ are normalized constructible. The same references show $C,D$ lie in $\mathcal I_{X'}$. Hence $a_K,b_K$ are isomorphisms between objects of the normalized full subcategory. For an arbitrary $M\in\mathcal I_X$, both $v_I^*F_{f,I}M$ and $F_{f',I}u_I^*M$ belong to $\mathcal I_{Y'}$ by [det-sp-integral-direct-image-tower] and the pullback result.

source.place: Proof (3), right-adjoint normalization, reconstruction comparisons and identification of the integral transpose

proof.text:
Under $r_{Y'}$, the required integral exchange at $M$ is the following actual map between its two reductions:
$$g_M=\sigma_{f',u_I^*M}^{-1}F_{f'}(\alpha_{u,M}^{-1})\,\beta_{r_XM}\,V(\sigma_{f,M})\,\alpha_{v,F_{f,I}M}.$$
All factors are invertible. For any $A,B\in\mathcal I_T$, [det-sp-normalized-equivalence] gives the inverse on Hom sets explicitly by $g\mapsto\iota_B^{-1}L_T(g)\iota_A$. Indeed, $r_T\iota_A=\kappa_{r_TA}^{-1}$ and $r_T\iota_B^{-1}=\kappa_{r_TB}$ by the triangle identity, so reduction of this expression is $\kappa_{r_TB}r_TL_T(g)\kappa_{r_TA}^{-1}=g$ by naturality of $\kappa$. Naturality of $\iota$ proves that this formula also sends $r_T(h)$ back to $h$. Apply it to $g_M$ and $g_M^{-1}$ to obtain the unique $\beta_I(M)$ and its inverse. The formula for $g_M$ is natural in $M$, so faithfulness makes $\beta_I$ natural. Thus its reduction is exactly the prescribed coefficient transport of $\beta$.

source.place: Proof (3), right-adjoint normalization, reconstruction comparisons and identification of the integral transpose

proof.text:
Given the actual tower map $t_K:P_K\to Q_K$, put $g=b_K^{-1}t_Ka_K:r_{X'}C\to r_{X'}D$. Apply the Hom inverse in Step 4 at $X'$ to obtain
$$T_K=\iota_D^{-1}L_{X'}(b_K^{-1}t_Ka_K)\iota_C.$$
The same triangle and naturality calculation gives $r_{X'}T_K=g$ as an equality in the derived tower category. This is the unique lift. Since $t,a,b$ are natural, reduction of each naturality square for $T$ commutes, and faithfulness of $r_{X'}$ makes that square commute. No factor $t_K^{-1}$ is used.

source.place: Proof (3), right-adjoint normalization, reconstruction comparisons and identification of the integral transpose

proof.text:
Make the source and target identifications in the transpose formula explicit. Put $\sigma'_C=\sigma_{f',C}$ and $\alpha=\alpha_{v,K}$. The reduced integral transpose, as a map $F_{f'}P_K\to VR$, is
$$\alpha\,r_{Y'}(\varepsilon_{f',I,v_I^*K}F_{f',I}(T_K))\,(\sigma'_C)^{-1}F_{f'}(a_K^{-1}).$$
Substitute the counit formula of Step 2 for $f'$ and use naturality of $\sigma_{f'}$. This becomes
$$\alpha\,\varepsilon_{f',\bullet,r_{Y'}v_I^*K}\,F_{f'}(q_{f',v_I^*K}\,r_{X'}T_K\,a_K^{-1})
=\varepsilon_{f',\bullet,VR}\,F_{f'}(G_{f'}(\alpha)q_{f',v_I^*K}\,r_{X'}T_K\,a_K^{-1})
=\varepsilon_{f',\bullet,VR}\,F_{f'}(t_K).$$
The first equality is naturality of the tower counit from [det-sp-tower-gluing]; the second substitutes $b_K=G_{f'}(\alpha)q_{f',v_I^*K}$ and $rT_K=b_K^{-1}t_Ka_K$. This proves exactly the displayed transpose identity under its stated operation comparisons.

source.place: Proof (3), right-adjoint normalization, reconstruction comparisons and identification of the integral transpose

proof.text:
Reduce the other integral counit composite using the identical source and target identifications of Step 6. Naturality of $\alpha_v$ first gives
$$\alpha_{v,K}\,r_{Y'}(v_I^*\varepsilon_{f,I,K})=V(r_Y\varepsilon_{f,I,K})\,\alpha_{v,F_{f,I}J_fK}.$$
Invert the defining comparison formula for $\beta_I(J_fK)$ in Step 4, cancel $\sigma'_C$, and use $a_K=U(q)\alpha_{u,J_fK}$. The entire reduced composite is therefore
$$V(r_Y\varepsilon_{f,I,K})\,V(\sigma_{f,J_fK}^{-1})\,\beta_{r_XJ_fK}^{-1}\,F_{f'}(U(q^{-1}))
=V(\varepsilon_{f,\bullet,R})\,V(F_f(q))\,\beta_{r_XJ_fK}^{-1}\,F_{f'}(U(q^{-1}))
=V(\varepsilon_{f,\bullet,R})\,\beta_{G_fR}^{-1}.$$
The first equality is Step 2. For the last equality apply naturality of $\beta:VF_f\to F_{f'}U$ to $q:r_XJ_fK\to G_fR$: it says $\beta_{G_fR}V(F_f(q))=F_{f'}(U(q))\beta_{r_XJ_fK}$; invert the isomorphisms and cancel. This verifies the right-hand side of the desired equation with its specified $\beta_I$.

source.place: Proof (3), right-adjoint normalization, reconstruction comparisons and identification of the integral transpose

proof.text: If $t$ satisfies the assumed tower counit equation, Steps 6 and 7 identify the reductions of the two integral composites after the same invertible source and target comparisons. Cancel those comparisons. Faithfulness of the equivalence $r_{Y'}$ of [det-sp-normalized-equivalence] then proves equality of the integral composites themselves. This proves the asserted integral counit equation for arbitrary natural actual $t$, with no invertibility hypothesis on $t$.

split_report.summary: Kept the full statement and statement dependencies. Proved counit-preserving right-adjoint normalization, actual tower reconstruction, unique exchange lifting, and both reduced transpose composites explicitly. Reused existing results, including the Mathlib right-adjoint uniqueness leaf; no new nodes. Checked the cited statements and comparison directions; no levelwise faithfulness is assumed.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes det-sp-tower-exceptional-bc proof (3), specifically right-adjoint normalization, the two reconstruction comparisons, and the equality of transposes. The unit route (tower adjunction followed by normalized reconstruction) is unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Generic base-change stability of smoothness and its relative dimension establishes that f-prime meets the hypotheses of the same adjunction lemmas; it does not replace a step of the purity unit.

Supplies the already specified integral right adjoint J_f to the same compact-support functor, for the counit-preserving uniqueness comparison with H_f; the unit gives H_f but does not specify this independent adjoint.
